authority: Uttarakhand Forest Department & Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve Directorate
title: Mandatory Annual Winter Park Closure
description: Valley of Flowers National Park is legally closed to all visitors from November 1 to May 31 each year. The region is buried under 10-15 feet of snow with active avalanche risk. Entry is strictly prohibited under Wildlife Protection Act 1972.

evidence.sourceTitle: Uttarakhand Forest Department — Park Access Regulations
evidence.verificationNote: Mandatory annual winter closure from Nov 1 to May 31 confirmed by Uttarakhand Forest Department.

authority: South Western Railway (Hubballi Division) — Railway Protection Force
title: Permanent Railway Track & Bridge Trekking Ban (Jeep Safaris Operational)
description: Walking on the Dudhsagar railway tracks and bridge is permanently illegal under Railway Act — punishable by fines and arrest by the Railway Protection Force. Jeep safaris via Collem inside Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary reopened in October 2026 for the 2026–27 tourist season. Viewpoint access by authorised jeep safari is fully operational. Only unguided railway-track access remains prohibited year-round.

evidence.sourceTitle: Dudhsagar Falls Current Status — MyGoa365 (October 2026 Reopening Confirmed)
evidence.issuingAuthority: South Western Railway (Hubballi Division) — Railway Protection Force
evidence.verificationNote: Dudhsagar Falls and jeep safaris officially reopened for 2026–27 tourist season in early October 2026 (confirmed by MyGoa365 and GoaKhabar Live video). Railway track trekking remains permanently illegal under RPF enforcement.

authority: South Wayanad Forest Development Agency (VSS) & Kerala Forest Dept
title: Monsoon Landslide Safety Suspension
description: All trekking permits to Chembra Peak and Hridaya Saras are suspended during peak Southwest monsoon due to severe landslide vulnerabilities, soil liquefaction, and extreme leech infestation.

evidence.sourceTitle: Kerala Forest Department — Chembra Peak Trekking Permits
evidence.verificationNote: Seasonal permit suspension during monsoon confirmed by Kerala Forest Dept and DTPC Wayanad.

title: Coracle Boating & Gorge Bathing Ban
description: Coracle boat operations and waterfall gorge bathing are officially banned when Kaveri river inflow from Mettur/KRS exceeds 18,000 cusecs. Tourists can only view cataracts from the high watchtower bridge.

evidence.effectiveFrom: Triggered by Kaveri inflow >18,000 cusecs (July–August typically)
evidence.verificationNote: Ban trigger threshold (18,000 cusecs) is widely reported; official DDMA order URL not confirmed. This is a condition-based restriction, not a fixed calendar closure.

authority: Jog Management Authority / Karnataka Tourism Police
title: Gorge Descent Stairs Closed for Safety
description: The 1,400-step stone staircase to the bottom of the falls is closed to prevent slips on algae-covered wet steps and respiratory distress from high-velocity mist. Top viewpoints remain fully operational.

evidence.sourceTitle: Jog Falls — Shivamogga District Tourism Official Page
evidence.verificationNote: Staircase closure during monsoon is well-documented by Karnataka Tourism; official seasonal order URL not confirmed.

authority: Vashisht Gram Panchayat & Kullu District Tourism Authority
title: Permanent Civilian Access Shutdown — Gram Panchayat & Tourism Authority Order
description: Civilian access to the sacred Jogini Waterfall trek is permanently shut down and prohibited by the local village council (Vashisht Gram Panchayat) and Himachal Pradesh tourism authorities. The shutdown was initiated due to persistent safety hazards along slippery cliff paths, fatal slipping incidents, and ecological degradation caused by mass tourism. Google Maps lists the site as permanently Closed. The restriction applies year-round.

evidence.sourceTitle: Jogini Waterfall — Google Maps (Status: Closed, Manali, Bashisht, HP)
evidence.issuingAuthority: Vashisht Gram Panchayat / Kullu District Tourism Authority
evidence.verificationNote: Google Maps and local tourism authorities confirm Jogini Waterfall is permanently closed. Gram Panchayat and Himachal Pradesh tourism authorities have initiated a full shutdown due to safety hazards on cliff paths and ecological damage from mass tourism. Year-round restriction applies — not limited to monsoon months.

title: Zero Visibility Dense Fog & Landslide Advisory
description: Cherrapunji receives torrential rains (>2,000 mm/month) causing persistent cloud cover that often results in 0% waterfall visibility for days at a time. Mudslide risks exist on the Shillong-Sohra bypass.

evidence.sourceTitle: Meghalaya Tourism — Nohkalikai Falls Visitor Information
evidence.verificationNote: Fog advisory is consistent with Cherrapunji's documented annual rainfall patterns (IMD normals); official MTDC advisory URL not confirmed.

title: Monsoon Cloudburst & Landslide Highway Hazard
description: Trekking is strongly discouraged due to Dehradun-Mussoorie-Sankri road blockages from falling debris, swollen mountain torrents, and continuous flash-flood threat.

evidence.sourceTitle: USDMA — Monsoon Landslide Hazard Warnings (Uttarkashi/Sankri Area)
evidence.verificationNote: USDMA issues monsoon hazard warnings for Uttarkashi-Sankri road annually; specific advisory URLs for 2025-26 not confirmed.

authority: J&K Forest Dept, Ganderbal District Administration & Indian Army (15 Corps)
title: Blanket Security Prohibition & Administrative Clearance Suspension
description: High-volume alpine trail operations suspended indefinitely due to pending administrative clearances and military security crackdowns. Blanket prohibition bars civilian access to Vishansar, Gadsar, and 30-50 offbeat Kashmir destinations.

evidence.sourceTitle: Kashmir's Trekking Ban Left a Legal Fight in Its Wake — Kashmir Observer
evidence.issuingAuthority: J&K Forest Department & Ganderbal District Administration
evidence.verificationNote: Confirmed non-operational status documented across Trekup India, The Searching Souls, Kashmir Observer, and The Wire.

title: Summer Shola Grassland Fire Hazard Advisory
description: Dry vegetation during peak summer increases wildfire risk. Daily trekker entries are restricted to 200 visitors, and afternoon ascents after 12:00 PM are halted.

evidence.sourceTitle: Kerala Forest Department — Meppadi Range Wildfire Advisories
evidence.verificationNote: Summer fire-season entry restrictions for Chembra are documented by Kerala Forest Dept; specific advisory URL not confirmed.
